Create an issue in the following format to add an Accessibility Mode that increases the font size and some icon sizes to make it more visible to users with visual impairments or small screens: Summary

Users need a way to get their transaction data out of Actual Budget and into external tools (Excel, Google Sheets, tax software, a financial advisor's template). Right now there is no one-click export at the account level; users must either use the budget-level export or manually copy data. Adding a "Download as CSV" button to each account's transaction view gives individuals and small businesses a frictionless path to their own data.

User Story

As a user reviewing my checking account, I want to click "Export to CSV" so that I can open my transactions in a spreadsheet without manually copying them.

Rough Scope

Medium — CSV serialization is straightforward, but for a beginner team the real work is locating the right component to add the button to, understanding how transaction data is accessed in that view's context, and handling edge cases like an empty account or a filtered transaction list vs. the full account. Navigating an unfamiliar codebase to find and confidently modify the right file takes meaningful time.

Source

Personal use / original idea from the assignment brief

1	#!/bin/sh
2	# Shared agent guard for shell/Bash commands (Claude PreToolUse[Bash],
3	# Codex PreToolUse[^Bash$], Cursor beforeShellExecution via adapter).
4	#
5	# Deterministically enforces the project's git-safety and workspace rules that
6	# used to live as prose in AGENTS.md / .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md.
7	# Reads the command from `.tool_input.command` on stdin. Exit code 2 + stderr
8	# blocks the call and feeds the reason back to the agent.
9	#
10	# Best-effort by design: it catches the honest mistakes agents actually make
11	# (plain push-to-main, a forgotten [AI] commit prefix, --no-verify, yarn in a
12	# workspace). It does NOT try to defend against deliberate evasion via unusual
13	# shell forms (git global options before the subcommand, `git commit -F`/`-C`/
14	# `--amend`, etc.) — CI and branch protection are the real gates for what lands.
15	
16	block() {
17	  echo "$1" >&2
18	  exit 2
19	}
20	
21	# Fail closed: a malformed payload (jq parse failure) blocks rather than allows.
22	cmd=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty' 2>/dev/null) ||
23	  block "Blocked: could not parse the hook payload (.tool_input.command)."
24	[ -z "$cmd" ] && exit 0
25	
26	# Enforce: always run yarn from the repo root, never in a child workspace.
27	# Catch cd/pushd into a package dir, or `yarn --cwd packages/...`.
28	case "$cmd" in
29	  *"cd packages/"* | *"cd ./packages/"* | *"cd packages "* | *"cd ./packages "* | \
30	    *"pushd packages/"* | *"pushd ./packages/"* | *"pushd packages "* | *"pushd ./packages "* | \
31	    *"yarn --cwd packages/"* | *"yarn --cwd ./packages/"* | *"yarn --cwd packages "* | *"yarn --cwd ./packages "* | \
32	    *"yarn --cwd=packages/"* | *"yarn --cwd=./packages/"* | *"yarn --cwd=packages "* | *"yarn --cwd=./packages "*)
33	    case "$cmd" in
34	      *yarn*)
35	        block "Blocked: run yarn from the repo root, not a child workspace (AGENTS.md). Use 'yarn workspace <name> <cmd>' from the root instead." ;;
36	    esac ;;
37	esac
38	
39	# Everything below only applies to actual git invocations. Match `git` as a
40	# whole token (not a substring) so commands that merely mention git — e.g.
41	# `rg "git config" AGENTS.md` — aren't falsely blocked.
42	is_git=0
43	set -f
44	for tok in $cmd; do
45	  [ "$tok" = "git" ] && {
46	    is_git=1
47	    break
48	  }
49	done
50	set +f
51	[ "$is_git" -eq 1 ] || exit 0
52	
53	# Never skip git hooks.
54	case "$cmd" in
55	  *--no-verify* | *--no-gpg-sign*)
56	    block "Blocked: skipping git hooks (--no-verify/--no-gpg-sign) is forbidden." ;;
57	esac
58	
59	# Never change git config (reads are fine).
60	case "$cmd" in
61	  *"git config"*)
62	    case "$cmd" in
63	      *--get* | *--list* | *" -l "* | *" -l") ;;
64	      *) block "Blocked: 'git config' changes are forbidden." ;;
65	    esac ;;
66	esac
67	
68	# Never force-push or push to main/master.
69	case "$cmd" in
70	  *"git push"*)
71	    case "$cmd" in
72	      *--force* | *" -f "* | *" -f")
73	        block "Blocked: force push only on explicit user request. Use --force-with-lease and confirm with the user first." ;;
74	    esac
75	    # Match main/master only as a whole ref/token (padding avoids matching
76	    # branches like "maintenance" or "main-feature"). Also catch explicit
77	    # refspecs like `HEAD:refs/heads/main` / `origin refs/heads/master`.
78	    case " $cmd " in
79	      *" main "* | *" master "* | *":main "* | *":master "* | \
80	        *" refs/heads/main "* | *" refs/heads/master "* | \
81	        *":refs/heads/main "* | *":refs/heads/master "*)
82	        block "Blocked: never push to main/master. Push the feature branch instead." ;;
83	    esac ;;
84	esac
85	
86	# Commit messages must start with [AI].
87	case "$cmd" in
88	  *"git commit"*)
89	    # The [AI] rule applies to the commit subject, which git takes from the
90	    # FIRST -m/--message flag (later -m flags become body paragraphs, e.g. a
91	    # Co-Authored-By trailer). ${var#pattern} strips the shortest matching
92	    # prefix, i.e. finds the first occurrence; when both flag spellings are
93	    # present, the longer remainder is the one whose flag came first.
94	    rest=''
95	    case "$cmd" in
96	      *" --message"*)
97	        rest=${cmd#*" --message"}
98	        rest=${rest#=} ;;
99	    esac
100	    case "$cmd" in
101	      *" -m"*)
102	        m_rest=${cmd#*" -m"}
103	        [ ${#m_rest} -gt ${#rest} ] && rest=$m_rest ;;
104	    esac
105	    # First line of the remainder tells us the message form. An empty result
106	    # means no inline message (editor/--amend/-F) — left alone.
107	    first=$(printf '%s\n' "$rest" | sed -n '1s/^[[:space:]]*//p')
108	    msg=''
109	    case "$first" in
110	      *'$('*'<<'*)
111	        # Heredoc via command substitution: -m "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)".
112	        # The subject is the first non-blank line of the heredoc body (git's
113	        # default cleanup strips leading blank lines).
114	        msg=$(printf '%s\n' "$rest" | sed -n '2,$p' |
115	          sed -n '/[^[:space:]]/{s/^[[:space:]]*//;p;q;}') ;;
116	    esac
117	    # Inline string: strip one leading quote, truncate at the next quote
118	    # (good enough for a prefix check). Also the fallback when the heredoc
119	    # pattern matched but no body line followed — e.g. a single-line <<<
120	    # here-string — so a statically unknowable message fails closed instead
121	    # of slipping past as empty.
122	    [ -n "$msg" ] || msg=$(printf '%s\n' "$first" | sed "s/^['\"]//; s/['\"].*//")
123	    case "$msg" in
124	      "" | "[AI]"*) ;;
125	      *) block "Blocked: commit messages must start with '[AI]'. Got: $msg" ;;
